reasons.reason: Amylase is an enzyme that cuts the bonds linking glucose units in starch, so as I chew, it is already splitting starch into maltose and short dextrins before anything gets swallowed.
The reason to start breaking starch down in the mouth is to free sugar early, and the thin, blood-rich lining under my tongue can take small molecules straight into circulation for quick glucose.
I treat it as a tipping rod: gravity's torque acts at the midpoint, half the length from the base, so the center of mass starts falling with half of free-fall acceleration.
At the moment I let go the rod is still essentially vertical, so gravity's torque about the base is close to nothing and the floor's push still balances the weight, leaving no net acceleration.
A dielectric weakens the field between the plates by a factor of K, and since the capacitor's storage depends on that field, my conclusion is that the capacitance falls by the same factor.
With the same charge on the plates, the dielectric cuts the field and so the voltage by K, and since capacitance is charge over voltage, I get a capacitance K times larger.
The field at the center goes as current divided by radius. Halving the current halves it, and doubling the radius halves it again, which leaves me with a quarter of the original.
Doubling the radius also doubles the length of wire producing the field, which offsets the greater distance, so the only net change I see comes from halving the current, giving half the field.
As the aircraft picks up speed, its wake gets swept back over the body and fuselage drag climbs steeply, so to me the power needed to keep accelerating is what has to be managed.
At low airspeed during transition the rotors can settle into their own downwash, and I know that recirculating wake is what creates vortex ring state, with its sudden loss of lift and control.
In general relativity gravity is the geometry of spacetime rather than a force, and I understand mass bends that geometry so that time itself runs slower deeper inside the well.
A black hole born from a collapsing star keeps an intense magnetic field, and that field stores enormous energy near the horizon, which in relativity adds to the warping that slows my clock.

Heat kills by unfolding proteins and breaking membranes, and that damage speeds up exponentially with temperature, while acid mostly just holds growth back, so for me temperature sets the actual kill rate.
Salmonella cannot multiply in a strongly acidic product, so the acid alone keeps the population from ever building up, which tells me the heat step is not what really achieves the required reduction.
Frequency of a mass on a spring goes as the square root of stiffness over mass, so when I make the mass four times larger, the frequency is divided by the square root of four.
The spring constant sets how stiff the oscillator is, and nothing changed it here. A heavier mass just hangs lower at equilibrium, so I expect it to bounce at the same rate as before.
Force per unit length on a wire perpendicular to the field is current times field strength, so when I double one factor and halve the other, the product comes back to where it started.

My reasoning is that the field is what pushes on the moving charges, so halving it halves the force, while doubling the current mainly means the same charges drift faster rather than more push per length.

Fat arriving in the duodenum makes the intestine release cholecystokinin, which I learned slows stomach contractions and tightens the pylorus, so fatty meals sit longer while bile and enzymes catch up.
Fatty acids in the duodenum signal that digestion is underway, and I'd expect vagal reflexes to step up peristalsis so the stomach moves chyme along faster to where bile and lipase do their work.
Counting the stages of decay, I go from all of the carbon to half and then down to a quarter, which is three levels in total, so I multiply 5730 years by three.
Twenty-five percent is a quarter, which is one half times one half, so I count exactly two half-lives, and two times 5730 years gives the age of the fossil.
In clean daytime air the hydroxyl radical attacks sulfur dioxide and turns it into sulfuric acid vapor, which I know is so nonvolatile that it nucleates into new particles as sulfate aerosol.
Sulfate forms in the same polluted plumes where nitrogen oxide chemistry runs, and I connect those oxides forming strong acids with pulling sulfur dioxide into the acidic aerosol particles.
Focal length is set by the curvature of the lens surfaces, and putting the lens in a liquid does not reshape the glass, so I would say the geometry and the focal length stay put.
How much a lens bends light depends on the index difference between glass and its surroundings. In this liquid that difference shrinks a lot, so I get much weaker bending and a more distant focus.

Centripetal acceleration measures how fast the velocity changes direction, and here I have the full 200 meters per second being redirected continuously, so the acceleration matches that speed in size.
I use the formula of speed squared over radius: 200 squared is 40,000, and dividing that by the 1000 meter radius gives the centripetal acceleration directly.
Surface forces scale with length while gravity scales with volume, so when I shrink the channel to micrometers the surface term wins by orders of magnitude and controls how the fluid moves.
Shrinking the channel shrinks both effects together, since less liquid means less weight but also less surface pulling on it, so to me the two forces scale down side by side and stay balanced.
